summary: Iter92 end-to-end tests for Firebase Cloud Messaging integration. Backend: /app/backend/tests/test_iter92_fcm.py — 13/13 pytest cases pass covering /api/push/fcm/{register,devices,test}, settings PUT/GET for fcm_prefs (all 7 keys), _fcm_notify_company triggered by kiosk kasgeld (pref ON → fake token auto-cleaned after Google rejection; pref OFF → token stays, no send), kiosk-token cannot register (401/403), and existing PWA /api/push/* endpoints untouched. Frontend: logged in demo@surirent.sr → /my-awesome-rentals-bv/admin/notifications renders fcm-section with 7 switches (payment, overdue, approval, kasgeld, employee, maintenance, invoices), fcm-devices-empty visible, fcm-test-btn present AND disabled (no devices), tap-sounds-section still rendered, PWA push-enable testid present. Fixed one unrelated pre-existing 500 in GET /api/kasgeld that blocked the frontend page (sort key mixing str/float caused by seed payment with float created_at).
critical_code_review_comments: backend/server.py `_list_cash_compute`: payments.created_at may be stored as a float (unix epoch from legacy/test seeds) while kasgeld.created_at is ISO string → sort crashed with TypeError. Patched to coerce `_sort_at` to str; main agent should consider normalising created_at to ISO at insert time instead of just str-coercion in sort.

backend/server.py `_fcm_notify_company` uses `data.get('kind')` to resolve the pref — kinds not in _FCM_KIND_PREF (e.g. generic/system notifications) silently never push to FCM. Intentional per spec but worth guarding/logging unknown kinds.

backend/server.py `_fcm_admin` returns 403 only when the user is logged in as a non-admin via get_current_user; kiosk-token has no admin user context, so request falls through to get_current_user→401 (Bearer missing). Tested as 401/403 — both acceptable.

frontend/src/components/AndroidAppMeldingen.jsx `toggle` sends the FULL prefs object on every switch toggle (not just the changed key). Backend merge_section handles this fine but a partial update would be slightly cleaner.

success_rate.frontend: 100% visual (fcm-section + 7 switches + empty state + disabled test btn + tap-sounds + pwa push all render)

seed_data_creation: Each test registers TEST_dev_* fake FCM tokens (prefixed TEST_) via POST /api/push/fcm/register and auto-cleans them via a module-level autouse fixture plus the FCM endpoints themselves (Google replies UNREGISTERED → backend deletes). fcm_prefs reset to all-true at end of test run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Rerun: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iter92_fcm.py -v`. The test file is self-contained (fresh admin login + fresh kiosk PIN login via Anita). Pytest cleanup fixture removes TEST_dev_* devices. Frontend crash with /admin/notifications only happens on *second* goto in the same Chromium session — probably a Chromium-headless flakiness in this sandbox, not an app bug (page renders perfectly on first visit; see iter92_fcm.jpeg).
rca of the issue: One pre-existing 500 on GET /api/kasgeld was uncovered when the Notifications page tried to render (actually not caused by Notifications — some other hook pre-fetches /api/kasgeld). Root cause: in `_list_cash_compute` the merged list is sorted on `_sort_at` which equals `created_at`. Payments inserted via legacy/seed code store `created_at` as a Python float (`time.time()`), while kasgeld entries store it as an ISO string via `iso(now_utc())`. Python 3's sort cannot compare str and float, so sort() raised TypeError and the endpoint returned 500. Mitigation applied in server.py line 14886: `key=lambda x: str(x.get('_sort_at') or '')`. Permanent fix (recommended for main agent): coerce payments.created_at to ISO on write.
